says: `fabrika/package-imports` picks a file's part with `node:path`'s `matchesGlob`, which ignores case on macOS and not on Linux, so a part's glob can claim a different file on a laptop than on CI: `next/packages/libfabrika/**/*Test.ts` takes `Latest.ts` and every `.test.ts` on macOS.
proof: On macOS with Node 26.13.0, `node -e 'const p=require("node:path");console.log(p.posix.matchesGlob("a/Latest.ts","a/**/*Test.ts"), p.matchesGlob("a/b.test.ts","a/**/*Test.ts"), p.matchesGlob("a/Latest.ts","a/**/*[T]est.ts"))'` printed `true true true`. Linux CI matches with case, so the same file falls in another part there.
cost: A production file whose name ends in `test` case-insensitively passes lint on a laptop and fails on CI, and the rule's own law must keep such names out of its generated paths.
